claims.title: equation eq:itoY2 [proof]
claims.scope_note: The pathwise identity (4.5) is used only through its expectation. The proof of Lemma 4.1 takes expectations in it at each time t, which removes its three stochastic terms. The later bound on E sup|δY|² squares the forward form of the lemma's equation and applies BDG to the L² martingales ∫δZ dW and ∫∫δU dÑ, without (4.5). What the proof draws from the expectation is the weighted inequality of lines 193–199, the clause eq_supE_weighted of A:eq:supE, from which it derives the bound at every time and (4.6), the clause eq_supE. Both are stated and proved from the library's weighted second-moment identity for Itô–Lévy processes (Ito.SecondMoment.integral_exp_mul_self_eq_of_isItoLevyProcess, at the weight e^s), whose difference between the horizons T and t is, coordinatewise, the expectation of (4.5). That identity needs only the square integrability of δξ and the finite energy of δZ, δU and φ that the lemma assumes. The zero means of the three stochastic terms are the clauses of A:lem4.1:M2-infinite-activity. The pathwise identity itself is not stated. It would need an every-time Itô–Lévy formula for general predictable integrands, with local stochastic integrals because δY₋δZ and δY₋δU need not have finite energy, and no claim of the paper uses more than its expectation. The region (lines 126–137) is the sentence of (4.5): its lead-in 'Itô's formula for e^t|δY_t|² then gives the pathwise identity' (lines 126–127) and the display.
